title: Make controlled-contract assessment projection honor its declared byte bound

criteria: REOPENED DEFECT. WK-2461 was cancelled after proving only that workspace_controlled_contract_integration_test_design_query could traverse 52 gaps. That did not exercise the final workspace_controlled_contract_assess transport envelope. The live proof-assessment call still fails with controlled_contract_semantic_projection_invalid and the message `controlled-contract semantic projection cannot satisfy its declared byte bound`.

ROOT CAUSE. The core proof and integration assessment summary projectors independently fill a summary to the 8,192-byte delivery ceiling. The MCP adapters then add assessment_identity and, for proof assessment, workspaceRepo, and reapply the same ceiling. The final envelope can therefore exceed the declared bound after the omitted semantic population has already been snapshot-bound, causing a refusal that returns no usable assessment identity.

ONE FINAL-ENVELOPE OWNER. A shared assessment-response materializer in packages/wiki-mcp/src/lib/controlled-contract-tools.mjs owns the complete final MCP envelope for both assessment families because it knows every transport-added field. It reserves those fields once and supplies wiki-core an explicit remaining allowance for semantic summary selection. Wiki-core must not independently claim the full 8,192-byte allowance. The returned summary, identity, exact counts, omitted counts, and supported query route fit as one deterministic result.

DEC-0118 LOSSLESSNESS. The 8,192-byte summary and 16,384-byte page sizes are delivery bounds only, never content caps. Every omitted public semantic row and every value within it remains reachable through the returned assessment identity and the existing authenticated snapshot/cursor owner in packages/wiki-mcp/src/lib/controlled-contract-assessment-snapshots.mjs. A successful assessment may not create an inaccessible snapshot or require rerun, inference, reconstruction, repository reads, hidden state, or a second snapshot registry.

TASK-RELEVANT SEMANTIC ACCESS. Agents receive only the semantic summary and specific typed collection rows or typed row-field ranges needed for their task. workspace_controlled_contract_assessment_query and workspace_controlled_contract_integration_test_design_query remain the complete public paths. Non-task-relevant source-derived digest fields are not part of the public assessment result. Any retained lossy derived value must name an operative complete semantic source path. Router and tool descriptions identify the appropriate collection and continuation without sending rationale, raw contract text, or unrelated rows.

RAW-ROUTE OWNERSHIP. WK-2426 remains the sole owner of no raw registered transport, controlled-contract exclusion from generic spill, role posture, and enforced-filesystem confidentiality distinctions. WK-2461 consumes those invariants without restating or changing them and grants no raw carrier, artifact, join-graph, filesystem, or generic content-reference recovery route.

ASSESSMENT ENCAPSULATION VOCABULARY. Remove the three assessment raw-source completeness exemptions, the public assessment completeness_exemption member, and non-task-relevant source-derived fields including detail_digest, result_digest, population_digest, and requirement_digest; do not relabel them. Package collection descriptors define the task-relevant public semantic collections. Internal carrier, artifact, proof-plan, evaluation-input, and join-graph bytes remain outside the assessment public contract. Assessment-specific docs describe API encapsulation and context efficiency, not a security or confidentiality guarantee.

OVERSIZED PUBLIC VALUES. The existing assessment snapshot registry retains every complete task-relevant public row. The two existing query routes extend their typed pagination contract so a row need not fit one page: structured or nested values use typed field projection, and an oversized scalar uses authenticated offset/length ranged retrieval with an exact total, all bound to assessment identity, collection, row identity, snapshot currentness, and cursor expiry. Reassembly reaches the exact complete public value. Do not reject or cap producer content to satisfy a delivery limit, add a second paginator or registry, byte-cut, ellipsize, silently drop, raw-spill, or terminate without an operative continuation.

BOTH ASSESSMENT FAMILIES AND NON-AUTHORITY. Apply final-envelope and lossless-continuation invariants to workspace_controlled_contract_assess and workspace_controlled_contract_integration_test_design_assess plus their two query routes. Export one assessment non-authority value from the semantic assessment boundary and consume it for both assessment summaries and integration-design refusals. Preserve package assessment semantics, source currentness, authenticated snapshot/cursor behavior, collection ordering, selectors, and advisory-only semantics.

REGRESSION AND MUTATION COVERAGE. Final registered MCP-response tests cover N-1, N, and N+1 summary envelopes for both assessment families after all adapter fields are added; complete multi-page and oversized-row/field traversal; exact counts and totals; cursor expiry/currentness; a near-bound summary that previously lost its assessment identity; and mutants that double-budget, omit identity, omit a row or field segment, miscount, cap producer content, recreate a completeness exemption or removed digest field, add a second paginator, or reinstate assessment security/confidentiality rationale.

DURABLE GUIDANCE. docs/mcp-controlled-contract-operations.md owns semantic-operation wording and docs/mcp-integration.md owns transport wording. They state that raw assessment sources remain server-owned for encapsulation and context control, agents obtain complete task-relevant semantic results through summaries and typed query continuation, and failed final-envelope or value-continuation budgeting is a defect. docs/mcp-operation-reference.md remains an index and changes only if a link must change.

SCOPE AND NON-GOALS. This WK repairs assessment-family final-envelope budgeting, task-relevant public descriptors, semantic summary/page/field projection, the existing snapshot/query path, tests, discovery wording, and the two owning durable docs. It does not grant direct carrier or artifact access, change underlying controlled-contract or proof-pack evaluation semantics, alter proof authority or CCE, broaden role permissions, change WK-2426 raw-route/filesystem policy, add a second paginator or registry, or put runtime protocol guidance in AGENTS.md.
validation: Reproduce workspace_controlled_contract_assess at the pre-fix near-bound summary and prove the final response returns assessment_identity, exact counts, omitted counts, and the supported query route within the declared delivery bound.

Traverse every proof-assessment and integration-test-design semantic collection through the existing authenticated snapshot/cursor owner; reconcile rows and field/range continuations exactly to summary counts and totals with no duplicates, omissions, raw carrier fields, hidden reconstruction, content caps, or second paginator.
Run final-envelope N-1/N/N+1 tests after workspaceRepo and assessment_identity are materialized for both assessment families; inner-projector-only byte tests are insufficient.

Exercise a public row smaller than, equal to, and larger than the 16,384-byte page, including an oversized scalar and an oversized structured value. Prove typed field projection or offset/length ranged retrieval reconstructs the exact complete value with total, identity, snapshot, expiry, and currentness binding; no producer rejection, byte cut, ellipsis, spill, inaccessible snapshot, or terminal no-route refusal is allowed.

Mutation-test double budgeting, missing identity, incorrect totals, lost rows or field segments, invalid cursor/currentness, producer content caps, recreated completeness_exemption or source-derived digest output, a second paginator, duplicated non-authority literals, raw artifact recovery, and assessment security/confidentiality wording.

Run focused controlled-contract package descriptor, wiki-core assessment projection, existing snapshot registry, wiki-MCP registration/transport, tool-discovery, and documentation tests; run git diff --check, work-record validation, and workspace_generate_and_lint.
